Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming to iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful one: it will automatically change your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27 can repair compromised login credentials with your authorisation, powered by Apple Intelligence

A whole new era of Apple Intelligence is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and other companion software updates. One of the powerful new AI features involves the Apple Passwords app.

The Passwords app launched two years ago as a dedicated hub for login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

If there's an issue with a password in your database, the app has always alerted you. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach, or is reused across multiple accounts, Passwords will let you know.

But until now, you've still had to manually fix those problematic credentials yourself.

However, in iOS 27, Apple says its new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords for you in many situations. According to its website:

With this feature, you can always keep your login credentials safe, use strong passwords, and not have to worry or spend time doing it yourself.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and will roll out to all users in the coming weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to arrive in iOS 27.0, but availability in the beta has been unstable, so it may be delayed until iOS 27.1.

Have you used the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Feel free to share in the comments.
